rules.statement: Flags are flip-flops computed from the next pointer values (look-ahead), so each flag is exact at its own domain's clock edge and conservative only by the other side's pointer visibility.
m_vlsit_sfifo_wr owns the write pointer, write acceptance, full and full-threshold flags, overflow pulse, memory write port and write-side software reset FSM, in CLK-WR/RST-WR domain.
m_vlsit_sfifo_rd owns the read pointer, read acceptance, empty and empty-threshold flags, underflow pulse, memory read address (next read pointer) and read-side reset FSM, in CLK-RD/RST-RD domain.
m_vlsit_sfifo_top is a structural wrapper holding interface, parameters, interconnect and the three instances, with no state or storage.

rules.condition: At a rising edge of i_clk_wr with i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 0 and no software reset block
rules.statement: The word on i_wr_data is stored at the write pointer address, the write pointer increments, and flags are recomputed for the next cycle.
The read side uses the new write pointer at its next strictly later rising edge, directly or one edge later through the retiming flop.

rules.condition: When the read side uses the new write pointer
rules.statement: The read flag register and memory output register load at the same edge, so o_empty and the read data change together.

rules.condition: At a rising edge of i_clk_rd with i_rd_en = 1 and o_empty = 0
rules.statement: The word on o_rd_data is taken, the read pointer increments, and the output register loads the following word; the memory read address is the next read pointer's address.
The read pointer becomes visible to the write side at its next strictly later rising edge, directly or one edge later, where o_full may fall.
Occupancy (write pointer minus read pointer modulo twice the depth) stays between 0 and PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH.
No write is accepted while o_full is 1, and no read is accepted while o_empty is 1.
o_full is 1 whenever occupancy is PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH, and o_empty is 1 whenever occupancy is 0.
The write side never sees a read pointer ahead of the real one, and the read side never sees a write pointer ahead of the real one; views only lag.
Pointers and flags change only at a rising edge of the clock of their own domain.
